blocks.text: VALENCIA CITY, Bukidnon—The local government here has mobilized aggressive El Niño mitigation measures, shifting from broad blanket orders to data-driven, granular interventions and allotting a P140-million fund as state weather forecasters warn of a severe dry spell extending through mid-2027. The city has earmarked a flexible P140 million disaster management fund for next year, prioritizing immediate drought response initiatives, including the acquisition of water tanks, distribution hoses, and public service continuity plans. June Ray Valero, City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (CDRRMO) chief, said the local government unit is prioritizing localized responses to protect communities and safeguard public education from […]...
